answer: Requiring each agent identity to lock a refundable stake on-ledger turns fake accounts from free into costly. Like casting nets across an ocean, an attacker must spread limited funds ever thinner as every new identity demands its own stake. A single verified agent becomes an onyx-hard anchor: its bond can be slashed visibly on misbehavior, and every downstream transaction must trace back to that bonded vertex before the network grants access to shared services or escrowed payments.
